Yes. HTTP/3 runs over QUIC (RFC 9000), which is a transport protocol implemented on top of UDP. QUIC supplies its own reliability, congestion control, stream multiplexing, and TLS 1.3 encryption, so UDP serves mainly as a datagram carrier that middleboxes will pass.

Caveat: some networks block or throttle UDP/443, so clients typically fall back to HTTP/2 over TCP, usually discovered via the `Alt-Svc` header or HTTPS DNS records.
